stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
In a study of mouse lymph nodes, immunologist Rhea Okonjo's team counted germinal centers, the clusters where B cells refine the antibodies they produce. They found roughly half as many in aged mice as in young ones. Because B cells drive germinal-center formation, the team concluded that B cells lose this capacity with age.

Text 2
Using higher-resolution imaging, Tomas Lindqvist confirmed Okonjo's count. His images also showed that aged nodes contain far fewer follicular dendritic cells, which display the antigens B cells must encounter before forming germinal centers. A shortage of these cells could by itself limit germinal centers, Lindqvist notes, even if aged B cells remain fully capable.
choices: The lymph nodes of aged mice hold fewer of the sites where B cells refine antibodies than those of young mice do.
B cells in aged mice are less able than B cells in young mice to start forming new germinal centers.
A shortage of follicular dendritic cells is the main reason that germinal centers decline in aged mice.
Imaging at lower resolution probably overstated how few germinal centers the aged mice actually had.
explanation: Split Text 1 into its observation and its inference. The observation is that aged mice have about half as many germinal centers. The inference is that aged B cells lose the ability to form them. Lindqvist 'confirmed Okonjo's count', so he accepts the observation and challenges only the inference by naming another possible cause: too few follicular dendritic cells. The one thing both authors hold is the observation. Choice A restates it, using Text 1's definition of germinal centers as the clusters where B cells refine antibodies.

B.why: This is Okonjo's inference, not something both authors accept. Lindqvist says aged B cells may 'remain fully capable', and that is exactly the conclusion he is questioning. You picked the claim Text 1 ends on without checking whether Text 2 accepts it.

C.why: You saw that Text 2 offers another cause and then made it stronger than it is. Lindqvist only says the shortage 'could' limit germinal centers, so he doesn't call it the main reason. Okonjo blames the B cells, so she wouldn't agree with this either.

D.why: This is the trap for this subtype: you treated Text 2 as an attack on the data. The higher-resolution imaging confirmed the count instead of correcting it. Lindqvist disputes what the count means, not the count itself.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
When engineer Priya Haddad repeatedly loaded 3D-printed titanium brackets, they cracked after far fewer cycles than forged brackets did. Microscopy showed a small pore at the origin of nearly every crack. Haddad therefore concluded that porosity left by printing is what shortens the brackets' fatigue lives.

Text 2
Re-examining Haddad's brackets with high-resolution x-ray tomography, Felipe Arce did find pores at the crack origins. Yet those pores sit where unusually coarse grains meet, and such boundaries concentrate stress on their own. It is difficult to exclude, Arce argues, that the grain boundaries start the cracks and the pores simply happen to lie nearby.
choices: In the printed brackets, fatigue cracks tended to begin at locations where pores were present.
The pores left by printing are what cause the printed brackets to crack after fewer cycles.
Coarse grain boundaries, not pores, are what cause the printed brackets to crack early.
Ordinary microscopy mistook features at the crack origins for pores that were not really there.
explanation: Text 1's observation is that a pore sat at the origin of nearly every crack. Its inference, marked by 'therefore', is that porosity causes the early failure. Arce's tomography 'did find pores at the crack origins', so he accepts the observation. He then names another possible source of the same pattern: coarse grain boundaries that concentrate stress, with the pores 'simply' nearby. Both authors therefore agree only that cracks began where pores were, which is choice A.

B.why: This is Haddad's 'therefore' conclusion, and it is the claim Text 2 was written to challenge. Arce suggests the pores may just be nearby while the grain boundaries start the cracks, so he wouldn't agree with it.

C.why: You spotted Arce's alternative cause and then stated it as settled fact. He says only that it is 'difficult to exclude', which raises a possibility without proving it. Haddad blames the pores, so she would reject this choice as well.

D.why: This is the subtype trap: you read the new imaging method as overturning the old data. Arce's tomography confirmed that the pores were really there. He questions what they mean, not whether they exist.
